blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Route optimisation at network scale is not the same exercise as route optimisation at van level. At a thousand daily vans, the relevant questions become structural: where the depots are sited, how zones are assigned, how capacity is allocated between day and evening shifts, which customers deserve which service tier, and how the whole system re-balances when demand spikes in one region and collapses in another.

The real gains at this scale come from structure, not from individual cleverness. A well-placed depot is worth a hundred clever drivers. A well-assigned zone is worth a month of manual route adjustments. A well-designed shift pattern is worth more than any single piece of optimisation software.

Senior leaders who invest in these structural choices produce operations that are significantly cheaper, considerably more reliable, and far more pleasant to work in — without any of the heroic route-planning stories that impress nobody after a week.

items.q: According to the text, how does optimisation at network scale differ from optimisation at van level?
options: It abandons the idea of service tiers
The questions it asks become structural
items.why: "the relevant questions become structural" — mudam de nível, deixam de ser de rota individual.

items.q: What does the text say a well-placed depot is worth?
options: A single piece of optimisation software
A month of manual route adjustments
items.why: "A well-placed depot is worth a hundred clever drivers."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Structural choices drive most of the savings at scale.
Individual route-planning heroics are the key to lasting gains.
Depot placement matters more than driver cleverness.
Well-designed shift patterns beat optimisation software.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta contra o heroísmo individual — "impress nobody after a week".

items.q: The phrase "heroic route-planning stories that impress nobody after a week" suggests that…
options: clever individual fixes are impressive but not durable
storytelling should be part of every review
drivers rarely talk about their routes
such stories are the pride of the operation
items.why: Inferência: o brilhantismo pontual chama atenção no curto prazo, mas não sustenta o ganho.

items.q: What can be inferred about the author's view of optimisation software?
options: It is the single most important lever
It replaces the need for depots
It matters less than good structural design
items.why: Inferência: "worth more than any single piece of optimisation software" — a estrutura vem antes da ferramenta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentar o programa de rotas à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. What I'm putting in front of you today is not a set of clever routes — it's a network programme. Three changes, essentially. We relocate three depots, we redesign two shift patterns, and we replace a single zone-assignment rule that has quietly cost us for years.

Let me be precise about the numbers, because I know that's what you'll hold me to. Modelled across a full quarter, this cuts total miles by nine per cent — and, crucially, it holds. This isn't a good week that regresses to the mean; it's a structural floor that stays lower.

Now, I want to head off the obvious objection. Someone will say our current planners are excellent, and they are. But no amount of individual brilliance offsets a depot in the wrong place. A better-sited depot is worth considerably more than a month of manual adjustments — and it works while everyone sleeps.

The one thing I'd ask of this room is discipline. Re-balance the zones every quarter, resist the temptation to tinker between reviews, and let the structure do the work. If we do that, this is significantly cheaper and far more reliable — permanently.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Harry describe what he is presenting?
options: A network programme with three changes
items.why: "it's a network programme. Three changes, essentially."

items.q: What figure does Harry commit to, and what does he emphasise about it?
options: A cut he cannot yet quantify
A twenty per cent cut in headcount
A nine per cent cut in miles that holds over time
A nine per cent cut that appears only in a good week
items.why: "cuts total miles by nine per cent — and, crucially, it holds… a structural floor."

items.q: How does Harry handle the point that the current planners are excellent?
options: He says planners should be replaced by software
He disputes that they are excellent
He agrees, but says brilliance can't offset a badly-sited depot
items.why: "they are. But no amount of individual brilliance offsets a depot in the wrong place."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "it works while everyone sleeps"?
options: The system runs on a night shift only
The gain is automatic and needs no ongoing heroics
items.why: Inferência: a estrutura bem desenhada entrega o ganho sem esforço manual contínuo.

items.q: What does Harry's request for "discipline" imply about the main risk to the programme?
options: That the depots cannot physically be moved
That people will tinker between reviews and erode the structure
That the board will reject the budget
items.why: Inferência: pedir para não mexer entre revisões sinaliza que a ameaça é a intervenção ad hoc, não a estrutura em si.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The savings are structural, not tactical." Here structural means…
options: built into how the system is designed
items.why: Structural = estrutural: inerente ao desenho do sistema, não a ajustes pontuais.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Relocating the ___ closer to demand cut the average first-mile distance in half."
items.why: Depot = depósito: é a base física de onde saem as vans.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Premium accounts sit in a higher ___, with tighter delivery windows."
items.why: Service tier = nível de serviço: a faixa de promessa de entrega atribuída ao cliente.

items.q: "We re-balance the zones every quarter." To re-balance means to…
options: redistribute load so the zones stay evenly matched to demand
items.why: Re-balance = reequilibrar: redistribuir a carga para que nenhuma zona fique sobrecarregada ou ociosa.

items.q: "The gains come from structure, not from individual cleverness." Cleverness here refers to…
items.why: Cleverness = esperteza: o improviso brilhante de um indivíduo, oposto ao ganho estrutural.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de operações e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The COO still has to sign off on the depot moves." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new zone rule region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two depot managers pushed back on the shift redesign." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the re-balancing plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving a few metres off each route won't move the needle at network scale." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível no resultado.
